source: Interim template writer (CLAUDE.md §00.2–§00.4, CONTRACTS.md R3.1). Narrative order follows ICH E2A 'Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting' (1994) and the CIOMS/ICH E2A expectation that an expedited report narrative states who, what, when, seriousness, action taken, outcome and causality. Reporting obligations cited by the sentences come from the EMPOWER-Lung 1 protocol R2810-ONC-1624 Amendment 9 (data/public/empower_lung1_protocol_excerpt.json); the section and page numbers that appear in the text are passed in as facts by the caller, the protocol_ref fields below document which protocol page each sentence implements.
rationale: Generated text is allowed only if every sentence is assembled from structured facts and cites the evidence ids of the facts it used (CLAUDE.md §00: rules decide, text tools write, people confirm). Keeping every sentence, label, joiner and date format here as data means the Python code only fills slots: changing the wording is a table edit with a reviewable diff, not a code change. Each sentence lists variants in priority order; the writer uses the first variant whose 'when' conditions hold and whose slots (placeholders plus 'cite') are all present, and omits the sentence when none is, so a missing fact is never replaced by filler such as 'unknown'. The only sentence about absent data is the explicit 'Information still needed' sentence built from the caller's missing-information list. No sentence gives medical advice; every stated grade carries 'provisional, investigator to confirm' and every AESI mention carries 'possible AESI, investigator to confirm'.

formats.rationale: Timestamps render in UTC with the zone named so a sponsor reader in another time zone cannot misread them (CLAUDE.md §4.2: UTC everywhere). Date-only facts (YYYY-MM-DD) are shown unchanged.

labels.rationale: Plain-English words for coded fact values. cm_fields maps the protocol's required CM CRF fields (generic name, dose, dose unit, frequency, indication, start/stop date) to plain words when the caller passes SDTM variable names; any other string is shown as given. 'simulated' always appears next to simulated vitals (CLAUDE.md §13).

fragments.rationale: Reusable phrases rendered into a single slot (for example the protocol status of one medication) with the same variant rules as sentences.

validation.rationale: Checks validate_written applies to any WrittenText, including an LLM writer's output before it is accepted (CLAUDE.md §00 generated-text contract). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions applied to the sentence with quoted passages removed (quotes are checked separately: each must appear verbatim in a fact that the same sentence cites). Unquoted factual claims are not verified beyond their evidence ids (a documented limitation), which is why the template writer is the default and decision words (grade, seriousness, causality, AESI) must carry their qualifier.
